finding: 2 of 5 console users (carol.wanjiru, contractor-devops) can sign in without MFA. One is an external contractor.
remediation: Enforce MFA with an IAM policy that denies all actions without MFA; move workforce sign-in to IAM Identity Center.

finding: No documented risk assessment process, risk criteria or risk acceptance criteria. Risks are tracked informally in a team chat.
evidence: Interview: CTO; document request DR-03 returned nothing
remediation: Adopt a written risk methodology (likelihood x impact, 1-25) with acceptance criteria approved by top management; build the risk register.

finding: Security group app-servers (sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f60002) allows SSH/22 from 0.0.0.0/0 to production application servers. Added on 2026-09-02 by contractor-devops in a password-only console session; AWS Config detected it, ticket TT-412 is 43 days past its 7-day SLA (WP-07 DRF-05).
remediation: Remove the rule; use SSM Session Manager for admin access; add an AWS Config rule to detect recurrence.

finding: No Statement of Applicability. Annex A controls have not been selected or justified for inclusion or exclusion.
remediation: Produce the SoA from the risk treatment plan, justifying each of the 93 Annex A controls.

finding: No internal audit programme exists and no internal audit has been performed.
remediation: Define an audit programme; complete one full internal audit cycle before the Stage 2 audit.

finding: The only CloudTrail trail is single-region and has log file validation disabled. Activity in other regions is not logged and log integrity cannot be proven.
remediation: Convert to a multi-region organization trail with log file validation, KMS encryption and S3 Object Lock on the log bucket. See 04-control-narrative.

finding: GuardDuty is not enabled in either in-scope region (af-south-1, eu-west-1). There is no automated threat detection.
remediation: Enable GuardDuty in all regions; route findings via EventBridge to on-call.

finding: Access key 1 for contractor-devops is 215 days old (limit 90). The same user has no MFA (GAP-01). The key was used to create an orphan bucket (WP-05) and to stop the AWS Config recorder (WP-07).
remediation: Rotate or delete the key; replace long-lived keys with role-based temporary credentials; review whether the contractor still needs access.

finding: An incident response plan exists in draft but has never been approved or tested.
remediation: Approve the plan; run a tabletop exercise based on a credential-compromise scenario.

finding: IAM password policy is below baseline: minimum length 8 (baseline 14), symbols not required, no reuse prevention.
remediation: Update the account password policy; risk reduces further once SSO replaces IAM users.

finding: No periodic access reviews are performed. The contractor account has no end date recorded.
remediation: Introduce quarterly access reviews with documented sign-off; set expiry dates on contractor access.

finding: No security assessment of the video-consultation and SMS suppliers, both of which process patient data.
remediation: Tier suppliers by data access; send CAIQ-based questionnaires to critical suppliers; add security clauses to contracts.

finding: 2 of 8 S3 buckets were created by hand outside Terraform (console and CLI). Both hold patient data and lack the module's CMK encryption, versioning, access logging and classification tags. Nothing prevented or flagged them.
remediation: Move both buckets into Terraform or delete them after data review; add an SCP denying s3:CreateBucket outside the pipeline role; run the orphan diff weekly in CI.

finding: The s3-patient-data module claims to enforce access logging but exposes it as an input (variables.tf:26). The patient-uploads bucket turns it off (live/prod/main.tf:37) with no risk acceptance.
remediation: Hard-code access logging in the module and remove the variable; if log volume is a problem, use lifecycle expiry on the log bucket instead.

finding: A contractor's workflow change (PR #258) made Semgrep non-blocking and removed it from the deploy's dependencies. 16 days later a HIGH SQL injection in patient search (PR #264, app/patients/search.ts:41) deployed to production.
remediation: Confirm exploitability and fix or roll back #264 now; restore Semgrep as a required check and in deploy needs; add .github/ to CODEOWNERS with platform review required.

finding: Segregation of duties in the pipeline can be bypassed and was: admins are exempt, production allows self-approval, and 4 of 39 PRs reached main without a review by a second human (#241 protection lowered to 0 approvals, #248 bot-only, #255 author's second account, #262 admin override).
remediation: Enforce rules for admins; require code-owner and last-push approval and dismiss stale reviews; enable prevent_self_review on production; remove duplicate accounts; define a logged break-glass process for hotfixes.

finding: GitHub Actions logs are kept for the 90-day default and not exported. 12 of 39 Q3 deploys can no longer be evidenced, and every future audit period longer than 90 days will have the same gap.
remediation: Ship build logs and evidence artifacts to the log-archive bucket with Object Lock for at least 400 days.

finding: Continuous monitoring broke at every link in Q3: the Config recorder was stopped for 6 days without alerting; versioning-rule failures are never routed; two MFA alerts were never ticketed; the GAP-03 SSH ticket is past SLA. Only 2 of 6 drift events were resolved.
remediation: Alert on Stop/DeleteConfigurationRecorder; route every rule's NON_COMPLIANT results; auto-create tickets from alerts; report MTTR together with open-past-SLA counts.

finding: The DR region eu-west-1, which holds a copy of patient data, is outside the security baseline: EBS encryption by default is off, there is no AWS Config recorder, and GuardDuty is off (GAP-07).
remediation: Apply the same baseline to every region through an Organizations-wide Terraform stack; deny unused regions with an SCP.
